messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH | GPU pool gpool-prod-4 queue growth detected (>600 pending). Autoscaler attempted scale but hit max_nodes. Started alerting: 5xx spike + streaming latency >3s. @oncall paged.

alice: I’m on it. seeing sustained queue growth on gpool-prod-4 across us-west-2. autoscaler logs show repeated 'reached max_nodes' errors.

ben: Context — we rolled redwood-llama-13b-kvV2 to canary yesterday at 04:15 and promoted to 10% at 09:00. Early telemetry showed slightly higher kv-cache miss and larger KV cache entries per request (avg context tokens +25%). Could be related.

carla: Confirming: traffic to model variant redwood-llama-13b-kvV2 is causing avg GPU mem usage to climb ~15% and inference durations up ~18% -> throughput regression.

dave: Logs from autoscaler:```[2026-11-09T18:02:31Z] autoscaler: attempt_scale desired=18 current=16 max_nodes=16 ERROR: reached max_nodes, cannot scale further```

erin: And node boot times are long due to kvcache warmup:```kvcache_warmup: start node-27; warmup_time=112s; kv_entries=4.2M``` so even if we could scale, coldwarm penalty is heavy.

frank: Customer impact - Support dashboard: ~12 customers with elevated 5xx (rate limit/queue-drop) and ~25 higher latency alerts. One enterprise customer (acme-corp) reported degraded streaming for chatbots. Logged as Sev2 for now.

grace: Any chance to throttle non-critical routes? We could apply temporary per-tenant rate limits or circuit-breaker for long-context requests.

alice: Quick mitigation plan: 1) rollback the promoted kvV2 variant to kvV1 for prod traffic, 2) enable emergency route throttles for long-context (>16k) requests, 3) request soft quota bump with infra for additional nodes or move some traffic to gpool-prod-3 in another AZ.

carla: Rolling back model traffic to kvV1 now (starting canary rollback). deploy-bot:```Deploy starting: rollback redwood-llama-13b-kvV2 -> kvV1; user: carla; cmd: rctl rollback model redwood-llama-13b-kvV2 --to kvV1 --project prod```

deploy-bot: Rollback started at 18:12:05Z (op id: op-9853). Notifying router to change traffic splits.

ben: FYI the runtime still holds larger KV entries per request due to a bug in the kv-decode path — even after rollback nodes might continue to have warmup overhead until caches are evicted. Need to evict prefix cache on nodes if possible.

alice: Can we issue a targeted KV cache eviction on nodes in gpool-prod-4? That should drop memory and reduce warmup penalty for subsequent requests.

dave: Command to evict cache on nodes (low-level):```for n in $(gcloud compute instances list --filter="name~'gpool-prod-4'" --format='value(name)'); do ssh $n 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-kvcache && sleep 5'; done``` Not ideal but will clear runtime cache. Doing on a few nodes first.

frank: Please coordinate — evicting cache will cause short spike in CPU while rebuilding. Marking non-burst customers in support.

erin: Also, autoscaler config has soft_limit=16 and hard_limit=18 per policy for that pool. We can temporarily raise soft_limit to 20 to allow scaling if infra approves. Noting that account-level quota may prevent it.

grace: I’ve applied emergency throttles to /chat.stream for tenants with average ctx>12000 tokens: reduced concurrency to 2. That should trim queue growth gradually.

carla: Rollback is at 30% traffic now. Seeing slow decline in queue depth. Good sign. deploy-bot: Rollback proceeding — 60% at 18:23.

support-bot: Sent notification to affected customers with guidance: we’re investigating and mitigating; ETA 30–60m. Template: "We’ve detected elevated latency/errors for some chat endpoints; mitigation in progress. No data loss. Expect restoration within 1 hour."

alice: After rollback reached 100% (18:29) queue depth dropped ~40% but not back to baseline. Some nodes still show high mem due to kvcache entries. Proceed with targeted cache restart on two busiest nodes.

dave: Restarted redwood-kvcache on node-09 and node-11 at 18:31. Observed immediate drop in mem pressure on those nodes. Queue depth trending down slowly.

ben: Runtime note: we need a patch to avoid creating oversized KV entries on kvV2 when request metadata present. Opening issue and tagging for later. For now rollback mitigates.

erin: Infra asked for justification for increasing pool limits. I’ve opened a request with quota team (q-7231). They said 30–60m response. Meanwhile we can try moving a fraction of model traffic to gpool-prod-3 (less loaded) via routing override.

carla: Routing override deployed to move 15% of traffic from gpool-prod-4 -> gpool-prod-3 at 18:38. That shaved another ~12% off queue.

frank: Current impact summary: queue peaked ~650 pending, currently ~90 pending. 5xx rate reduced by ~70% since rollback. acme-corp still seeing partial streaming truncation earlier but now improved.

grace: Would recommend follow-ups: postmortem, revert kvV2 changes and re-run canary with smaller context test, and add autoscaler fallback to allow spillover across pools before hitting max_nodes.

alice: Agreed. Immediate actions completed: rollback done, emergency throttles applied, targeted cache restarts performed, routing override applied. Monitoring for stabilization for next 30m.

ben: Adding technical action items for postmortem: reproduce kvV2 memory growth locally, add guardrails in runtime to reject requests that inflate kvcache above X entries per request, and add autoscaler metric for 'queue growth due to model variant' to correlate model rollouts with pool pressure.

carla: Noting that the root cause is likely a combination: kvV2 produced larger per-request KV footprints + canary rollout increased overall load -> autoscaler hit configured max_nodes and cold warm times prevented quick recovery.

dave: Handing off to next oncall in 20m. leaving follow-ups in #incidents-pmo. If anything regresses escalate to eng-sre.

alice: Thanks all, great coordination. @grace please escalate billing/enterprise comms for acme-corp.

grace: On it. Sent update to acme-corp CSM.

frank: Will prepare incident communications and initial impact numbers for postmortem.

erin: Quota request approved at 18:57 (soft increase to 20 nodes) but we didn’t need it after rollback. Keep the request open until we finalize autoscaler policies.

carla: Follow-up checklist added in the incident board. Drafting postmortem timeline.

alice: Handing off to @frank (next oncall) — I’m going offline, ping if queue starts trending back up.

frank: Acknowledged. I’ll monitor for 2h and coordinate postmortem. Closing pager for now. :white_check_mark:
